All reported estimates are used exactly as signed to the claim direction: for direction -1, a positive value means the exposed group has stronger, more negative dependency than the comparator; for direction +1, a positive value means the exposed group has a higher/weaker dependency score.\n\nH16, the main MSI-high versus MSS comparison for WRN dependency, is now independently validated. The discovery estimate was +0.790 (95% CI 0.760 to 0.819), and the independent validation estimate is +0.807 with a very stringent independent interval from +0.759 to +0.855. The lower bound is far from zero and the effect is extremely large relative to the observed WRN dependency-score distribution. This firmly supports, within this supplied dataset, the dataset-level association that MSI-high status is associated with much stronger WRN dependency. It is not evidence of causality or external generalizability, but it is among the strongest findings in the study.\n\nH21, the adenocarcinoma-restricted MSI-high WRN comparison, is also independently validated. The validation estimate is +0.813 (independent CI +0.754 to +0.872), closely matching the discovery subgroup estimate of +0.784. This supports the interpretation that the WRN/MSI-high association is not confined to the non-adenocarcinoma remainder of the dataset and is robust within the dominant adenocarcinoma subset. I keep H21 accepted and close further context investigation because it has achieved independent confirmation and its role as a consistency check for H16 is fulfilled. H16 remains active as a central accepted claim.\n\nH12, SMARCA4 loss versus SMARCA4-intact SMARCA2 dependency, also has independent validation: discovery +0.784 (95% CI 0.765 to 0.803), validation +0.800 (independent CI 0.768 to 0.832). The validation interval excludes zero with large margin and confirms the direction and magnitude. I keep H12 accepted and close its investigation as a validated core association.\n\nAt this point, three of the four strongest main associations are independently validated: SMARCA4 loss with stronger SMARCA2 dependency (H12), KEAP1 loss with weaker NFE2L2 dependency (H17, already validated earlier), and MSI-high status with stronger WRN dependency (H16). The remaining large accepted main association is H15: TP53 wild-type status versus TP53 loss for USP7 dependency. H15 has very strong internal support: overall discovery estimate +0.802 (95% CI 0.782 to 0.822), CDKN2A-intact context +0.800 (R21), and CDKN2A-loss context +0.808 (R31). Nevertheless, it has not yet been independently validated. Given that it is accepted, extremely large, mechanistically coherent, and internally stable across CDKN2A contexts, independent validation of H15 is the highest-priority next evidence request when a validation opportunity arises.\n\nThe negative interaction and specificity work continues to support the specificity of the accepted effects. The WRN effect is not meaningfully modified by adenocarcinoma subtype (H38 rejected), and WRN dependency is not associated with BRCA2 loss (H39 rejected). SMARCA2 and USP7 effects were not meaningfully modified by tested co-alteration or pathway contexts (H23, H26, H29, H37, H40 rejected). NFE2L2/KEAP1 reversal was not modified by TP53 loss or lineage subtype (H42, H43 rejected). Constructed-marker controls for SMARCA2, WRN, USP7, and NFE2L2 were near null (H45-H48), which lowers concern that these large effects are generic artifacts of the constructed assay panels, although specificity against every possible dataset confounder cannot be proven.\n\nNegative findings remain important. Simple binary driver/amplification associations for BRAF V600E, KRAS mutation, ERBB2 amplification, PIK3CA mutation, and TMED10/ERBB2 were rejected. ARID1A main effect on SMARCA2 and MDM2 TP53-pathway associations, including CDKN2A-loss interaction, were rejected. EGFR amplification overall remains unresolved/deferred: the overall estimate was borderline and tested adenocarcinoma and KRAS-wild-type refinements were unconvincing, but H22 remains registered as a possible lineage-interaction test if EGFR is pursued further.\n\nThe most informative next scientific step is to obtain independent validation for H15 while simultaneously registering targeted robustness tests for H15 and H17. I have registered a USP7 TP53-wild-type comparison within KEAP1-loss cells to test whether the USP7 association persists when NRF2 pathway context changes, and a USP7 interaction by lineage subtype to test whether the effect differs between adenocarcinoma and non-adenocarcinoma. I also registered a NFE2L2 KEAP1-loss comparison within TP53-loss cells to test whether the reversed KEAP1-loss effect remains present in a p53-null context. These are dataset-level association tests, not causal tests. Existing untested claims H24, H27, H31, H32, H34-H36, H22, and the MYC-amplification outcomes H2, H5, and H11 remain useful for closing out secondary and negative-control exploration after H15 throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.

is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator

record.narrative:
All new values are interpreted exactly as signed to the hypothesis direction. For direction -1 claims, a positive signed estimate means the exposed group has a more negative dependency score, i.e. stronger dependency. For direction +1 claims, a positive signed estimate means the exposed group has a higher dependency score, i.e. weaker dependency.

The specificity tests largely preserve the interpretation of the four validated core associations rather than expanding them broadly. H72 is null for SMARCA4 loss and POLR2A dependency (signed estimate -0.005; 95% interval -0.024 to +0.014), so the large SMARCA4-loss effect appears specific to SMARCA2 rather than spilling into a general transcription-dependency effect. H73 is null for TP53-wild-type status and RPL11 dependency (+0.004; -0.016 to +0.024), supporting the view that the USP7 association is not simply a generic p53/proteostasis or ribosome-stress effect. H74 is null for a main KEAP1-loss effect on USP7 dependency (+0.009; -0.033 to +0.050), reducing concern that the TP53-wild-type USP7 association is confounded by KEAP1-loss co-alteration. H75 is small and imprecise for MSI-high and DHX9 dependency (+0.017; -0.017 to +0.052), supporting specificity of the MSI-high effect to WRN rather than a broad MSI association across dependencies. H78 is null for MTAP loss and USP7 dependency (-0.001; -0.041 to +0.039), and H83 is null for an aneuploidy interaction on the TP53-wild-type USP7 association (-0.014; -0.060 to +0.032), so these genomic-context alternatives are not supported.

The core-consistency refinements are strong. H76 shows that the MSI-high WRN association remains enormous among BRCA2-intact cells (+0.794; +0.764 to +0.825), complementing the earlier null BRCA2-loss main effect and indicating the WRN association does not require BRCA2-loss co-alteration. H77 shows the TP53-wild-type USP7 association is essentially unchanged among MYC-amplification-negative cells (+0.802; +0.780 to +0.823), indicating the effect is not an artifact of MYC co-alteration. I accept these as dataset-level consistency findings and close them as secondary confirmations of the central associations.

The new mechanistic screen mostly produced nulls except for PTEN loss. H79 found no meaningful interaction between MSI-high WRN dependency and high mutation burden (-0.026; -0.090 to +0.038), supporting an MSI/MMR-specific rather than generic mutational-burden explanation in this dataset. H80 is null/near-null for NF1 loss and KRAS dependency (-0.020; -0.049 to +0.009), so no RAS-wiring dependency signal emerged there. H83 was null as above. H82 gives a statistically significant negative interaction contrary to the positive hypothesized direction: high hypoxia appears to slightly attenuate the KEAP1-loss reversal of NFE2L2 dependency (-0.054; -0.102 to -0.005). Although the interval excludes zero, the magnitude is small relative to the main reversal near +0.80 and I do not regard this as a scientifically meaningful effect modification worth accepting or validating at this stage; therefore the original positive-direction interaction claim is rejected and closed.

The important new positive discovery is H81: PTEN loss is associated with stronger STAT3 dependency. The signed estimate is +0.267 with a 95% interval from +0.215 to +0.319, far larger than the typical null/precision bounds in these tests and very large relative to the STAT3 dependency distribution. This is a moderate-to-large dataset-level association and is scientifically meaningful under the 10% clinical-significance context. Given the multiplicity of exploratory comparisons, I do not treat it as validated or causal yet, but I accept it as a current dataset-level association and request independent validation. I also registered follow-up robustness and specificity tests for PTEN loss/STAT3, including batch, Cas9 activity, culture, subtype, PIK3CA interaction, and a KRAS specificity control.

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful

The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link

censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.

and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.

comparison cell.

hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response

the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep

evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

record.narrative: No due assessments are requested, so this stage registers new comparisons to continue focused follow-up on the newly validated PTEN-loss/STAT3-dependency association and to broaden biologically plausible exploration around RAS pathway, inflammation/STAT3, chromatin specificity, and under-tested outcomes (RIT1, TMED10, MDM2). Direction convention remains: for direction -1 claims, a positive signed estimate means the exposed group has a stronger, more negative dependency score than the comparator; anticipated_direction is the expected raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast, so -1 means an expected raw negative contrast and therefore stronger dependency in the exposed group. The PTEN/STAT3 follow-ups test whether the moderate-to-large PTEN association is independent of PIK3CA co-alteration, is modified by an inflammatory IFN-gamma-high state, and remains specific relative to other central p53/USP7/MDM2 axis dependencies. The new KRAS, STK11, and SMARCA4-loss comparisons are not causal claims; they are dataset-level association probes designed to identify new strong effects, null specificity controls, or meaningful context restrictions. All registered analyses use the supplied 2000-lung-cell-line dataset with Welch discovery intervals and will be judged by effect size, interval precision, consistency with existing findings, and the 10% clinical-significance context rather than by biological assumptions alone.

Iteration 6/25, stage analyze, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Select up to 12 existing claim references in run_analyses. This requests analyses now; previously tested comparisons reuse their data and give no new sample. New results enter the ledger after this form is accepted and are assessed in appraise. Any assessment in this form must use evidence already in the supplied ledger.

record.narrative:
All estimates are interpreted exactly as signed to the hypothesis direction. For these direction -1 claims, a positive estimate means PTEN-loss cells have a more negative dependency score, i.e. stronger dependency, than PTEN-intact cells. The central H81 finding, PTEN loss associated with stronger STAT3 dependency, was already independently validated and is now supported by several non-overlapping or partially overlapping internal contexts: batch A H84 +0.234 with interval +0.125 to +0.342; Cas9-activity-eligible H85 +0.224, +0.159 to +0.289; adherent culture H86 +0.262, +0.203 to +0.321; adenocarcinoma H87 +0.268, +0.206 to +0.330. These context estimates are smaller in point magnitude than the high-IFN subgroup but remain clearly positive, reasonably precise, and large relative to the STAT3 dependency distribution and the near-null specificity tests. I therefore accept them as dataset-level robustness findings and close them as completed context checks rather than as separate causal or generalizable claims.

H90 tests the PTEN-loss main effect among PIK3CA-intact cells and is robust: +0.267, +0.210 to +0.323. H88 tests whether PIK3CA mutation modifies the PTEN-STAT3 effect and gives essentially zero interaction: +0.001, interval -0.150 to +0.152, with a small PIK3CA-mutant exposed cell_n of 38. Because the interval is wide and the point estimate is negligible, I reject the PIK3CA interaction claim as unsupported; this does not rule out a PIK3CA-mutant-specific main effect, but the registered interaction question is null. The specificity controls are informative negative results: H89 PTEN loss versus KRAS dependency +0.013 raw direction? The signed estimate is -0.013 and interval -0.035 to +0.008, so no meaningful KRAS-dependency association; H93 MDM2 specificity -0.015, -0.043 to +0.014; H94 USP7 specificity +0.017, -0.031 to +0.065; and H95 KRAS mutation versus STAT3 -0.018, -0.042 to +0.007. All are small, near or below the 10%-of-outcome clinical-significance scale, and interval-compatible with null or biologically negligible effects. They reduce the possibility that PTEN loss is simply a broad dependency-altering state and support specificity of the STAT3 finding.

The most scientifically interesting new result is the inflammatory context. H91 shows a very large PTEN-loss STAT3-dependency effect among high IFN-gamma signature cells: +0.423, +0.319 to +0.526. H92 is the corresponding interaction, showing that this effect is meaningfully larger in the high-IFN context than in the complement: +0.212, +0.094 to +0.331. The magnitude of the interaction is non-trivial relative to the main effect and the STAT3 dependency distribution, but it is more fragile because it comes from a subgroup and interaction contrast. I therefore accept H91 and H92 as dataset-level discoveries, close H91 as a completed context estimate, keep H92 active, and request independent validation of H92. This is the most valuable validation target because confirming context modification would be more important than re-confirming the already validated PTEN/STAT3 main effect. These remain associations in the supplied dataset and do not establish causality, pathway mechanism, or external generalizability.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.

is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum

deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

record.narrative: All estimates are interpreted exactly as signed to the claim direction; for these direction -1 dependency claims, a positive estimate means the exposed group has a more negative dependency score, i.e. stronger dependency, while a negative estimate means the opposite. H15 is reconfirmed at its response deadline. The claim is that TP53-wild-type cells have stronger USP7 dependency than TP53-loss cells. Discovery gave +0.802 with a 95% discovery interval of +0.782 to +0.822, and independent validation gave +0.799 with independent interval +0.769 to +0.828. The two estimates are nearly identical, and the validation interval remains far above zero. This is a very large, reproducible dataset-level association, so I accept H15 and keep it closed. H6 is now fully negative. KRAS mutation versus KRAS-intact status for dependency_KRAS was +0.014 in discovery (-0.004 to +0.031) and, with independent validation, -0.001 (-0.026 to +0.025). The validation interval includes zero and the point estimate is essentially null, so I reject H6 and close it. The key new validation is H92, the IFN-gamma-high context interaction for PTEN loss and STAT3 dependency. Discovery supported stronger PTEN-loss STAT3 dependency in the high-IFN context relative to its complement: +0.212 with a 95% discovery interval of +0.094 to +0.331. Independent validation, however, was much smaller and imprecise: +0.041 with independent interval -0.140 to +0.222. The validation interval includes zero and even includes a modest reverse effect, although it also remains compatible with a positive interaction through its upper bound. Thus the discovery is not replicated well enough to remain accepted, but the validation is not decisive enough to declare a strong rejection. I therefore downgrade H92 to unresolved and keep it active. This changes the interpretation of H91: the high-IFN main effect of PTEN loss on STAT3 dependency (+0.423, interval +0.319 to +0.526) remains an accepted dataset-level subgroup association, but we should not present the high-IFN interaction as validated context modification. The supported validated core associations remain SMARCA4 loss with stronger SMARCA2 dependency (H12: discovery +0.784, validation +0.800), MSI-high status with stronger WRN dependency overall (H16: discovery +0.790, validation +0.807) and in adenocarcinoma (H21: discovery +0.784, validation +0.813), TP53-wild-type status with stronger USP7 dependency (H15 as above), KEAP1 loss with weaker NFE2L2 dependency (H17: discovery +0.796, validation +0.801), and PTEN loss with stronger STAT3 dependency overall (H81: discovery +0.267, validation +0.310), reinforced by context checks H84-H87 and H90. The most useful negative and specificity results are that PTEN loss is not meaningfully associated with dependency_KRAS (H89), dependency_MDM2 (H93), or dependency_USP7 (H94); PIK3CA mutation does not support a clear interaction (H88); KRAS mutation is not associated with STAT3 dependency (H95); and KRAS mutation shows no validated KRAS-dependency association (H6). These findings reduce the concern that PTEN loss is a broad dependency-altering state and strengthen the specificity of the PTEN/STAT3 main finding. Remaining unresolved uncertainty centers on whether the PTEN/STAT3 effect is truly enhanced by inflammatory IFN-gamma-high context or whether the discovery interaction was fragile due to the relatively small high-IFN subgroup. The most informative next analysis is to characterize the PTEN/STAT3 effect in lower-IFN contexts and with a broader IFN split. I therefore registered two follow-up claims: a PTEN-loss versus PTEN-intact main contrast in the lower top-quartile IFN complement, and a new IFN interaction using a median-like split above zero. If the low-IFN effect remains similar to the overall effect, the failed top-quartile interaction would be more plausibly due to instability or power limitations rather than true absence of context modification; if it is near zero, H91 would be better interpreted as a subgroup-specific discovery without validated interaction.

Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,

subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.

comparison cell.

hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.

request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator

independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

expectation

evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

record.narrative: All estimates are interpreted exactly as signed to the claim direction. For these direction -1 dependency claims, a positive estimate means the exposed group has a more negative dependency score, i.e. stronger dependency, than the comparator. H102 shows a clear PTEN-loss main effect in the lower-IFN context: +0.211 with interval +0.152 to +0.269. This is well within the large STAT3-effect range, far above the near-null specificity tests, and supports the interpretation that PTEN loss is associated with stronger STAT3 dependency even outside the high-IFN top-quartile context. I accept and close it as an internal context check. H104 is similarly clear in the high-SLFN11 subgroup: +0.272 with interval +0.198 to +0.346. That strengthens the PTEN/STAT3 main finding in an interferon-responsive biomarker context, so I accept and close it. H105 tests whether the PTEN effect is enhanced relative to lower-SLFN11 cells and is essentially null: +0.010 with interval -0.095 to +0.114. This is small and imprecise enough to reject the registered SLFN11 interaction claim as unsupported. H106 tests the PTEN main effect within PIK3CA-mutant cells: +0.268 with interval +0.127 to +0.409, but the PTEN-loss cell count is only 38. The point estimate is very similar to the PIK3CA-intact main effect and the earlier PIK3CA interaction was null, so despite sparse subgroup representation I accept this as an internal consistency check rather than as a new validated context-specific claim. H107 shows that PTEN loss remains associated with stronger STAT3 dependency in TP53-loss cells: +0.190 with interval +0.085 to +0.296. This supports partial independence from the p53/USP7 axis already established, although the point estimate is somewhat lower than the overall effect; because the registered claim is the subgroup main effect and its interval excludes zero, I accept and close it, while noting that a future TP53-loss interaction test could examine attenuation. H108 tests lineage modification and is null: +0.001 with interval -0.115 to +0.117. I reject it and conclude that lineage subtype does not provide evidence for differential PTEN/STAT3 behavior in this dataset. H101 tests whether the strong SMARCA4-loss signal extends to STAT3 dependency and is null: -0.005 with interval -0.032 to +0.022. This supports specificity of SMARCA4 loss for SMARCA2 rather than a broad STAT3 dependency effect, so I reject and close H101. H69 and H70 test MYC amplification among high MYC-expression cells for KIF18A and RPL11; both estimates are negligible and interval-compatible with null, so I reject them. H96 tests KRAS mutation versus KRAS RIT1 dependency in adenocarcinoma and is null: -0.004 with interval -0.026 to +0.017. H99 tests STK11 loss versus KRAS dependency and is null: -0.002 with interval -0.022 to +0.018. These are useful negative results that reduce concern that these pathway alterations are broad dependency-altering states. The only uncertain discovery is H103, the median IFN-gamma interaction: +0.115 with interval +0.012 to +0.219. It suggests stronger PTEN-loss STAT3 dependency in cells with IFN-gamma signature above zero than below zero, and the effect magnitude is potentially meaningful relative to STAT3 dependency variability. However, the lower bound is close to zero, the split is post-registered after an unstable high-IFN top-quartile interaction that failed independent replication, and interaction contrasts are more fragile. I therefore keep H103 unresolved and request independent validation. If H103 validates, inflammatory context modification would be better supported; if not, PTEN loss should be treated as broadly associated with STAT3 dependency without a reproducible IFN-gamma interaction. All conclusions remain dataset-level associations and do not establish causality or external generalizability.

record.narrative:
All estimates are interpreted exactly as signed to the claim direction. For these direction -1 dependency claims, a positive estimate means the exposed group has a more negative dependency score, i.e. stronger dependency, whereas a negative estimate means the opposite. H81 is reconfirmed at its validation response deadline. The claim is that PTEN-loss cells have stronger STAT3 dependency than PTEN-intact cells. Discovery was +0.267 with a 95% interval of +0.215 to +0.319, and independent validation was +0.310 with independent interval +0.231 to +0.388. The validation estimate is slightly larger, clearly positive, and precise enough to exclude null at the multiplicative interval level. Together with the accepted context checks in batch A, Cas9-activity-eligible samples, adherent culture, adenocarcinoma, PIK3CA-intact and PIK3CA-mutant contexts, high SLFN11, TP53-loss cells, and lower IFN context, this establishes PTEN loss as the strongest supported predictor of stronger STAT3 dependency in this dataset. It remains a dataset-level association, not a causal or generalizable statement.

The key new validation is H103, the median IFN-gamma interaction for PTEN loss and STAT3 dependency. Discovery gave +0.115 with interval +0.012 to +0.219, suggesting a modest positive interaction. Independent validation gave -0.0456 with interval -0.200 to +0.109. The validation estimate is opposite in sign, imprecise, and interval-compatible with null and moderate reverse effect. Combined with the failed replication of H92, where discovery gave +0.212 but independent validation gave only +0.041 with interval -0.140 to +0.222, the IFN interaction evidence is not robust. I therefore reject H103 as unsupported. H92 remains unresolved, but I defer further immediate work on IFN interactions because two different IFN splits failed to replicate and the high IFN main effect remains accepted as a subgroup estimate. The practical conclusion is that PTEN loss is broadly associated with stronger STAT3 dependency, but the data do not support a reproducible inflammatory IFN context modification.

H3 is also reassessed and rejected. The overall EGFR-amplification main effect was +0.025 with interval including zero, and the adenocarcinoma and KRAS-intact subgroup estimates were also small and null. The effect is at or near a marginal scale and lacks internal replication, so it is better classified as a negative specificity result rather than an accepted EGFR dependency association.

Supported core dataset associations are now: SMARCA4 loss with stronger SMARCA2 dependency; MSI-high with stronger WRN dependency overall and in adenocarcinoma; TP53 wild-type with stronger USP7 dependency; KEAP1 loss with weaker NFE2L2 dependency; and PTEN loss with stronger STAT3 dependency. The validated core set is strong, whereas interaction evidence remains weak or unsupported. Important negative and specificity findings include: PTEN loss is not meaningfully associated with dependency_KRAS, MDM2, or USP7; SMARCA4 loss is not associated with STAT3 dependency; KRAS mutation is not associated with KRAS dependency after validation or with STAT3 or RIT1 in adenocarcinoma; MYC amplification among high MYC expression is not associated with KIF18A or RPL11; STK11 loss is not associated with KRAS dependency; PIK3CA, lineage, SLFN11, and IFN interaction tests are not supported.

Next, the most informative analyses should shift from IFN interaction pursuit to testing whether accepted core effects are context-modified by other strong axes. I registered three new interactions: PTEN loss and STAT3 dependency within TP53-loss context to test attenuation of the PTEN effect independent of the p53/USP7 axis; SMARCA4 loss and SMARCA2 dependency within KEAP1-loss context to test independence from the KEAP1/NFE2L2 axis; and TP53-wild-type USP7 dependency within STK11-loss context to test independence from the STK11/LKB1 axis. I also deferred lower-priority null-like EGFR, ERBB2, KRAS, TMED10, MYC main-effect, and other exploratory claims so that the next analyses can focus on mechanistically targeted context checks. All conclusions remain internal to the supplied 2000-cell-line dataset.

Iteration 8/25, stage analyze, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;

Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

For all new direction -1 main claims, a positive signed estimate means the exposed group has a more negative dependency score, i.e. stronger dependency, than the comparator. For all new direction +1 main claims, a positive signed estimate means the exposed group has a less negative dependency score, i.e. weaker dependency, than the comparator. For direction -1 interaction claims, a positive signed estimate means the exposed effect is stronger in the specified subgroup than in its complement. The population remains the supplied 2000 lung-cell-line dataset, and these are association hypotheses, not causal claims. First, I follow up the PTEN-loss/STAT3-dependency association in STK11-loss context. STK11/LKB1 and PTEN are common co-alterations in lung cancer, and STK11 loss may alter growth-signaling, metabolic state, or chromatin/immune-associated cell states that could modify STAT3 dependency. The interaction test asks whether PTEN loss is associated with an especially strong STAT3 dependency in STK11-loss cells; the STK11 main-effect test asks whether STK11 loss alone is associated with stronger STAT3 dependency. Plausible alternatives include independence from PTEN, STK11, or both, or a context-specific but small interaction. Second, I test receptor tyrosine kinase alterations as new STAT3-dependency predictors. EGFR amplification and ERBB2 amplification can activate STAT3 biology through receptor-associated kinase and downstream signaling, so a negative raw contrast would indicate stronger STAT3 dependency in amplified cells. The EGFR test restricts to KRAS wild-type cells to reduce confounding by alternative MAPK activation; the ERBB2 test is left unrestricted. Plausible alternatives include near-null receptor amplification effects, which would reinforce the current specificity of STAT3 dependency for PTEN loss rather than broad kinase-pathway amplification. Third, I broaden exploration to less-tested dependency axes. RB1 loss is a strong cell-cycle regulator and may increase vulnerability to mitotic or replication-stress-associated dependencies; I test dependency_KIF18A as a focused mitotic-kinesin outcome. NF1 loss is a negative-regulator loss in RAS pathway biology; I test dependency_RIT1 with direction +1 because NF1 loss may bypass upstream RAS-activator dependency and therefore be associated with weaker, less negative RIT1 dependency. BRAF V600E is tested against KRAS dependency among KRAS wild-type cells with direction +1 because BRAF-mutant MAPK activation may reduce dependence on KRAS itself. These are useful negative or new positive discovery tests rather than refinements of the current accepted core. Finally, I add a SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2 interaction with STK11 loss to test whether the large SMARCA4-loss effect is independent of the STK11 axis. Expected effect sizes are judged relative to the dependency outcome scales: established core effects are very large, whereas meaningful new associations should either be clearly larger than the observed null-scale estimates and approach a 10% or greater relative effect on the outcome scale, or be robust context modifications for an already strong accepted association. H102 shows a clear PTEN-loss main effect in the lower-IFN context: +0.211 with interval +0.152 to +0.269. This is well within the large STAT3-effect range, far above the near-null specificity tests, and supports the interpretation that PTEN loss is associated with stronger STAT3 dependency even outside the high-IFN top-quartile context. I accept and close it as an internal context check. H104 is similarly clear in the high-SLFN11 subgroup: +0.272 with interval +0.198 to +0.346. That strengthens the PTEN/STAT3 main finding in an interferon-responsive biomarker context, so I accept and close it. H105 tests whether the PTEN effect is enhanced relative to lower-SLFN11 cells and is essentially null: +0.010 with interval -0.095 to +0.114. This is small and imprecise enough to reject the registered SLFN11 interaction claim as unsupported. H106 tests the PTEN main effect within PIK3CA-mutant cells: +0.268 with interval +0.127 to +0.409, but the PTEN-loss cell count is only 38. The point estimate is very similar to the PIK3CA-intact main effect and the earlier PIK3CA interaction was null, so despite sparse subgroup representation I accept this as an internal consistency check rather than as a new validated context-specific claim. H107 shows that PTEN loss remains associated with stronger STAT3 dependency in TP53-loss cells: +0.190 with interval +0.085 to +0.296. This supports partial independence from the p53/USP7 axis already established, although the point estimate is somewhat lower than the overall effect; because the registered claim is the subgroup main effect and its interval excludes zero, I accept and close it, while noting that a future TP53-loss interaction test could examine attenuation. H108 tests lineage modification and is null: +0.001 with interval -0.115 to +0.117. I reject it and conclude that lineage subtype does not provide evidence for differential PTEN/STAT3 behavior in this dataset. H101 tests whether the strong SMARCA4-loss signal extends to STAT3 dependency and is null: -0.005 with interval -0.032 to +0.022. This supports specificity of SMARCA4 loss for SMARCA2 rather than a broad STAT3 dependency effect, so I reject and close H101. H69 and H70 test MYC amplification among high MYC-expression cells for KIF18A and RPL11; both estimates are negligible and interval-compatible with null, so I reject them. H96 tests KRAS mutation versus KRAS RIT1 dependency in adenocarcinoma and is null: -0.004 with interval -0.026 to +0.017. H99 tests STK11 loss versus KRAS dependency and is null: -0.002 with interval -0.022 to +0.018. These are useful negative results that reduce concern that these pathway alterations are broad dependency-altering states. The only uncertain discovery is H103, the median IFN-gamma interaction: +0.115 with interval +0.012 to +0.219. It suggests stronger PTEN-loss STAT3 dependency in cells with IFN-gamma signature above zero than below zero, and the effect magnitude is potentially meaningful relative to STAT3 dependency variability. However, the lower bound is close to zero, the split is post-registered after an unstable high-IFN top-quartile interaction that failed independent replication, and interaction contrasts are more fragile. record.narrative:
All estimates are interpreted exactly as signed to the registered claim direction. For direction -1 main contrasts, a positive signed estimate means the exposed group has a more negative dependency score, i.e. stronger dependency, than the comparator; for direction +1 main contrasts, a positive signed estimate means the exposed group has a less negative dependency score, i.e. weaker dependency. Direction -1 interaction positive signed estimates mean the exposed effect is stronger in the named subgroup.

H92 is the top-quartile IFN-gamma interaction for PTEN-loss/STAT3 dependency. Discovery gave +0.212 with a 95% interval of +0.094 to +0.331, suggesting a large positive interaction. Independent validation gave +0.041 with an independent interval of -0.140 to +0.222. The validation estimate is much smaller, imprecise, and interval-compatible with no interaction, even though it remains positive. This pattern, together with the failed replication of the median-split IFN interaction H103, makes the IFN interaction evidence unstable. I do not accept H92 as a robust interaction claim; I keep it unresolved but close further work because two different IFN splits failed to provide reproducible interaction evidence. The practical conclusion remains that PTEN loss is associated with stronger STAT3 dependency broadly, without reliable evidence for IFN context modification.

H6 tested whether KRAS-mutant cells have stronger KRAS dependency than KRAS-wild-type cells. Discovery was +0.014 with interval -0.004 to +0.031, and independent validation was essentially zero: -0.0008 with interval -0.026 to +0.025. Both are near the null scale for KRAS dependency and not meaningful. I reject and close H6 as a negative specificity result: KRAS mutation is not associated with altered KRAS dependency in this dataset.

H114 tested EGFR amplification versus STAT3 dependency among KRAS-wild-type cells under the original stronger-dependency direction. Discovery was -0.044 with interval -0.086 to -0.001, which was opposite to the registered stronger-dependency direction but just excluded zero. Independent validation was -0.022 with interval -0.084 to +0.040, i.e. smaller and null-compatible. The registered original claim therefore remains rejected, and I close it. Because I had registered a reverse claim H120 for EGFR amplification being associated with weaker STAT3 dependency in KRAS-wild-type cells, I also reassess H120: its discovery signed estimate was +0.044 with interval +0.001 to +0.086, but validation was only +0.022 with interval -0.040 to +0.084. The reverse finding is small, borderline, and not replicated with independent uncertainty, so H120 is also rejected and closed. This leaves EGFR amplification as unsupported as a robust STAT3-dependency predictor in this dataset.

H106 tested PTEN-loss/STAT3 dependency specifically within PIK3CA-mutant cells. Discovery was +0.268 with interval +0.127 to +0.409, based on a small PTEN-loss cell count of 38. Independent validation was +0.270 with independent interval +0.068 to +0.472. The validation estimate is almost identical to discovery and excludes null at the independent multiplicative level, despite the sparse subgroup. This supports the robustness of the PTEN-loss effect across PI3K-pathway contexts. I accept H106 as an internal consistency/context check and close it.

The supported core dataset associations remain: SMARCA4 loss with stronger SMARCA2 dependency; MSI-high with stronger WRN dependency overall and in adenocarcinoma; TP53 wild-type with stronger USP7 dependency; KEAP1 loss with weaker NFE2L2 dependency; and PTEN loss with stronger STAT3 dependency. The PTEN/STAT3 association is further supported in PIK3CA-mutant context by H106 and in many internal contexts by accepted subgroup/eligibility checks. Interaction evidence remains weak: IFN interactions do not replicate, STK11/KEAP1/TP53 modifications of the core axes are unsupported, and lineage interactions are null.

Important negative and specificity findings include: KRAS mutation is not associated with KRAS dependency, STAT3 dependency, or RIT1 dependency in adenocarcinoma; EGFR amplification is not a robust STAT3-dependency predictor in KRAS-wild-type cells after validation; ERBB2 amplification is null for STAT3; RB1 loss is null for KIF18A; NF1 loss is null for RIT1; BRAF V600E is null for KRAS dependency in KRAS-wild-type cells; and several interactions around PTEN/STAT3 are unsupported. These negative results reinforce that the accepted associations are pathway-specific rather than broad cell-line dependency-state effects.

Unresolved uncertainty is now mainly the isolated H92 IFN top-quartile interaction, which I close as unresolved rather than accepted, plus untested deferred claims such as MYC-amplification effects. The next most informative work is to characterize specificity and pleiotropy of the accepted predictors. I keep the MYC amplification main effects on DHX9, KIF18A, and RPL11 active, and register new specificity tests: PTEN loss effects on dependency_ERBB2 and dependency_EGFR, KEAP1 loss effect on dependency_STAT3, and TP53-wild-type effect on dependency_STAT3. These tests are expected mostly to be null-scale if the accepted axes are highly specific, and would be useful to confirm that specificity. All conclusions remain dataset-level associations, not causal or externally generalizable claims.

For direction -1, a positive signed estimate means stronger dependency in exposed group; for direction +1, positive means weaker dependency. Second, I test cognate receptor dependencies in adenocarcinoma KRAS-WT cells, where alternative MAPK bypass is absent, for ERBB2 and EGFR amplification; amplification is expected to strengthen the corresponding receptor dependency. Many expected alternatives are null-scale; only effects substantially larger than current null-scale estimates, preferably near or above a meaningful relative difference, should be considered scientifically important. These proposals complement active MYC and specificity tests without requesting validation.
